item.title: Dollar Falls to Weakest Since May on Waller Comments, Yen Surge
item.description: The dollar sank to the lowest level since May after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller noted progress on inflation and as the yen surged against its major counterparts.

item.title: Pentagon Says Its Anthropic Ban Is On, Despite Lutnick Remarks
item.description: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said Anthropic PBC has resolved its long-running issues with the Trump administration but a top Pentagon official begs to differ.

item.title: Chicago Projects $882 Million Budget Gap on Bond, Pension Costs
item.description: Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson is projecting an $882 million budget deficit for 2027, even as his administration continues to seek ways to close this year’s shortfall, underscoring the financial pressures facing the third-largest US city.

item.title: NYC Transit Agency Prepares $785 Million Mansion Tax Bond Sale
item.description: New York City’s transit network is planning to offer $785 million of debt backed by a levy on sales of luxury real estate.

item.title: Carney Says He’s Open to US Pact if Auto, Steel Terms Are Competitive
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney said a trade deal with the US is still possible, but only if the terms keep Canadian automotive and steel operations competitive.

item.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceXAI Hit by Service Outages for AI Models
item.description: OpenAI, Anthropic PBC and SpaceXAI were hit by outages on Thursday, according to user reports and company status pages, disrupting customers of three of the leading US AI model makers.

item.title: EU Risks Falling Further Behind US, China, Ireland’s Martin Says
item.description: Europe needs a change in mindset on innovation and technology and must take bolder action or it will fall further behind economic powerhouses like the US and China, according to Ireland’s prime minister.

item.title: The Fed Fights Over the Right Sports Analogy
item.description: Waller pushes back on Warsh.

item.title: Senate Considers Letting Contractors Hack Computers for Military
item.description: Contractors would be allowed to conduct military hacking operations with US government approval under a Senate defense bill that would mark the first time Congress has explicitly authorized the private sector to conduct offensive cyber missions.

item.title: DeepMind’s New AI Weather Model Goes Hourly for Power Markets
item.description: The newest AI weather model from Google DeepMind not only forecasts how hard the wind blows at turbine height and how much sunlight reaches a solar farm, but refreshes those projections every hour from satellite images.

item.title: Nscale Backs Robot Firm Figure Alongside $3.5 Billion Cloud Deal
item.description: Nscale struck a deal to supply at least $3.5 billion worth of AI cloud computing capacity to the robotics startup Figure, while also investing an undisclosed sum in the company.

item.title: Hungary Is Said to Pause Interest Rate Cuts and Lower Inflation Goal to 2.5%
item.description: Hungary’s central bank is set to halt interest rate cuts later this month as policymakers prepare to lower the highest inflation target in the European Union, according to a person familiar with the matter. The forint surged against the euro.

item.title: Your ETF of the Moment: Riding the Wild, War-Fueled Oil Market
item.description: The US-Israel war with Iran and the inability of Donald Trump to extricate himself from it have made one fund a good bet.

item.title: US Services Pick Up, Price Gauge Jumps to Four-Year High
item.description: The US service sector expanded in August by the most in six months, bolstered by strong demand and a pickup in business activity.

item.title: Chipmaker Longsys Said to Price Hong Kong Listing at HK$236
item.description: Shenzhen Longsys Electronics Co. priced its Hong Kong listing below the top end of the marketed range, according to people familiar with the matter, joining a wave of Chinese companies along the artificial intelligence supply chain to debut in the city.

item.title: Treasuries Rise After Fed’s Waller Notes Inflation Progress
item.description: Treasuries rose after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he’d be inclined to leave interest rates unchanged as long as inflation continues to slow.

item.title: Tyson Cuts Profit Outlook Again as Beef Segment Worsens
item.description: Tyson Foods Inc. cut its outlook for the fiscal year again as it sees more pressure from its beef segment.

item.title: Saudi Arabia’s Humain Unveils AI Model Based on China’s MiniMax
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s artificial intelligence company Humain has built a national AI platform based on an open model from Chinese lab MiniMax Group Inc., joining a growing list of countries seeking tighter control of the increasingly important technology.

item.title: HTC Brings $499 Vive Eagle Smart Glasses to US Amid Broader Privacy Concerns
item.description: HTC Corp. is rolling out its Vive Eagle smart glasses in the US, entering a market where category leader Meta Platforms Inc. is already facing mounting concerns from consumers over clandestine camera recording.

item.title: Iceland Data Center Costs Widen Current Account Gap to 2008 High
item.description: Investments in Icelandic data centers boosted the Atlantic country’s current account gap to the widest level since its financial crisis 18 years ago.

item.title: Russia’s Oil Revenue Sinks to Six-Month Low as Urals Price Drops
item.description: Russia’s oil revenue slumped to a six-month low in August, reflecting lower export prices and compounding pressure on the Kremlin’s ability to finance its war in Ukraine.

item.title: India RBI Faces About $11 Billion Bill on Foreign Deposits Plan
item.description: India tapped its vast diaspora for a record $127 billion through a special deposit program, a fundraising bonanza that economists say could come with a hefty $10.6 billion bill for the country’s central bank.

item.title: US Stock Futures Rise as Traders Parse Fedspeak, Earnings
item.description: US stock futures posted modest gains Thursday as bond yields stabilized near multi-year highs and investors digested latest commentary from Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller. Chip stocks fell after Broadcom Inc.’s results.

item.title: Saudi Firm Humain Eyes $2.5 Billion Fund to Build Data Centers
item.description: Artificial intelligence firm Humain is planning to raise an initial $2.5 billion from global and domestic investors for a fund to invest in data centers in Saudi Arabia, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Campbell’s Shares Slump on Sales Slide, Dividend Cut, Outlook
item.description: Campbell’s Co. shares slumped after the packaged food and snack maker said sales shrank for a fourth straight quarter, cut its dividend and unveiled a cost-savings plan.

item.title: US Trade Gap Widens to Largest Since Early 2025 on AI Push
item.description: The US trade deficit widened sharply in July to the largest since early 2025, reflecting a surge in imports of computers and other technology equipment.

item.title: US Share of Canada’s Exports Drops to 66%, Lowest Outside Pandemic
item.description: Canada’s trade surplus narrowed sharply in July, driven by lower exports of gold and energy, particularly to the US.

item.title: Fed’s Waller Says September Rate Decision Hinges on August CPI
item.description: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said his next decision on interest rates will be “heavily influenced” by August inflation data due next week, adding it may not take much to nudge him toward supporting a rate hike at the Fed’s upcoming policy meeting.

item.title: Investors Predict More Pain for Brazil Insurer After 90% Wipeout
item.description: Investors see few reasons to be optimistic about Hapvida, the Brazilian health insurer and hospital operator plagued by rising costs, constant litigation and an escalating debt load.

item.title: Blackstone’s BCRED Caps Redemptions Again After 10% Seek to Exit
item.description: Blackstone Inc. again limited redemptions from its flagship private credit fund after investors sought to pull 10% of shares, providing an early glimpse at the lasting quarterly withdrawal pressure ahead for the $1.8 trillion market.
